properties.name: OBSERVED 2026-10-25 on flo2.io (reflow2 0.91.0): from 18:48 UTC the Shop sample's calls hit the gateway's 30 s limit for 35 minutes while one engine thread stayed at 100% CPU. A write the caller was told was refused ("Nothing was changed") was in the design afterwards. A container restart at 19:22 cleared it. Root cause not yet walked
properties.statement:
OBSERVATION ONLY; NO CAUSE IS CLAIMED. The root-cause skill is to be run.
- flo2.io connector_calls for design 671a764fa790c030: read_my_design_back refused at 18:48:06 UTC after 30,074 ms. From then until 19:16, add_change_event (11 calls), get_node, loop_status and read_my_design_back were mostly refused at 30.0-30.3 s. Some fast calls (search_design, closure_report, building-model reads) still answered in under 1 s. Two writes answered ok at about 22 s and 19 s. Calls to other designs in the same window answered normally (e.g. add_requirement on dad8f529 in 1.9 s).
- On the droplet at 19:17-19:20: `docker stats` showed reflow2 at 100% CPU. `top -H` showed one tokio worker at about 91%, with 6 min 19 s of CPU time. Memory was 472 MiB of 7.76 GiB, with no swap. The container was healthy by its own check the whole time.
- The engine log had no panic and no error naming the stall, only ordinary refusals (derived relation "reruns_owed" not declared; `steps` naming use_helper_tool).
- `docker restart reflow2` at 19:22:48 (Anthony's word, "restart the reflow2 engine"): healthy in about 8 s, 0% CPU after. loop_status on the Shop then answered at once.
- chg:shop-sample-redo-of-model-measures-and-drawings-session-2026-10-25 is in the design, although every attempt the designer saw was answered "refused ... Nothing was changed". The gateway's 30 s timeout did not stop the engine, and the write landed later.
- Session 5 also saw a hand-off file saved while the design "could not record it".
TO ESTABLISH: what the pinned thread was computing (candidates: read_my_design_back or loop_status on a design that grew from about 490 to about 600 nodes that day; propagate_change reaching 527 nodes); why a computation outlives its caller; why later calls to the same design waited behind it; and why a timed-out write is reported as not written. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018ibUbMKCS1yK5W17cncp9P
